name_note: The literature uses both the current name Cutibacterium and the older name Propionibacterium for these skin bacteria.

sentences.text: Cutibacterium is a genus of Gram-positive skin bacteria whose best-known member, Cutibacterium acnes, was formerly named Propionibacterium acnes.
On facial skin, C. acnes and Staphylococcus epidermidis are the most prominent bacteria, and their relative abundance shifts with skin site, age and health status.
The species grows on skin lipids: an artificial sebum system enhances its growth, and it secretes the lipid-responsive lipase GehA.
Published work recognises C. acnes as a factor in acne vulgaris and in infections of prosthetic medical devices.
Other members matter clinically too; Cutibacterium avidum is described as an emerging opportunistic pathogen of prosthetic joint and breast implant infections.
